reasons: [reasoning_validity/major] D1 [furtherResearchThatCouldChangeConclusion[0]; counterarguments[3]; alternatives[0]; compare CL12/K15 and edgeCasesAndFailureModes[1]] The first item in furtherResearchThatCouldChangeConclusion says a rebalance dip below about 12% 'would make QueueForge a clear pass under a 50 ms SLO'. That ignores the draft's own post-failure steady state. Once rebalancing finishes the cluster runs on 5 nodes, and K15/CL12 estimate about 283k msg/s at the sub-50 ms point (340k x 5/6), which is below 300k. A small rebalance dip therefore does not give a pass if 300k must hold through node loss, because 5-node steady-state capacity is a separate condition. The same gap shows in the C3 counterargument response and in the alternatives entry 'right choice if... PoC shows the dip is much smaller'.

[reasoning_validity/major] D2 [verdict (final sentence); practicalImplications[0]; alternatives[2]; C2 weaknesses[2]] The bars for the two products are inconsistent. The verdict and practicalImplications[0] say StreamCore can be reconsidered if testing shows a gain of 'at least 36%' (K5). That gain only reaches exactly 300k msg/s, with zero headroom and nothing for failures. Meanwhile C2 calls QueueForge's 13.3% headroom 'thin' for a durable system. The StreamCore reopen threshold should include the same headroom and failure margin, roughly 300k/(1-margin), not just reach parity. The verdict also calls this a 'replication-CPU fix of at least 36%', but K5 is a throughput gain. Replication CPU savings and throughput are not 1:1, and the CPU-bound note (E3) does not quantify the relationship.

[decision_usefulness/major] D3 [verdict (condition a); edgeCasesAndFailureModes[0]; practicalImplications[4]] The verdict makes QueueForge's qualification depend on whether the requester 'can tolerate a backlog for 10-20 minutes', but the backlog is never sized, even though the inputs are available. At a 40% dip from 340k (204k served against 300k offered) the deficit is 96k msg/s. Over 600-1,200 s that is about 57.6M-115M messages (about 58-115 GB at 1 KB). Draining it with the 40k msg/s sub-50 ms surplus takes about 1,440-2,880 s (24-48 min) after the rebalance ends, and longer if the 5-node capacity is below 340k (K15 suggests it could be below 300k, in which case the backlog never drains). Without these numbers the requester cannot answer the question the verdict hinges on, and producer buffer sizing cannot be judged.

[coverage/major] D4 [criteriaAssessments C5; CL10; C5 strengths[0]] Storage capacity and retention are missing from C5. At about 900 MB/s of cluster writes under RF3, the cluster accumulates about 77.8 TB/day (about 13 TB/node/day on 6 nodes, about 15.6 TB/node/day on 5). Whether 6 nodes is realistic depends heavily on retention, and a domain expert would expect it for a durable broker at this rate. The draft covers only bandwidth (K3, K11, K12) and says the load is 'modest relative to commodity server hardware'. That statement holds for throughput but is unexamined for capacity. Consumer read egress, which may be several times ingest with multiple consumer groups, is also mentioned only as an exclusion and never estimated.
D4/D5 remedy includes research, but retention and benchmark methodology are requester/benchmark-internal facts not obtainable by search (E12: no external sources exist)
